subject: botany_2
question_text: Write in brief how plants synthesize amino acids.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.23, printed question 14. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Examiner audit revision (2026-09-05): the insider note no longer claims an examiner can read the enzyme off the equation, because neither printed equation carries an enzyme name; it now names both enzymes directly.

insider_note: Two named processes and two named enzymes. Write both equations, and write the enzyme name beside each one: glutamate dehydrogenase for reductive amination, transaminase for transamination.

steps.label: The two ways
steps.margin_note: Name both routes in the first three lines.
lines: Plants make amino acids in TWO ways:
steps.why: Naming both routes first means the rest of the answer only has to explain them, and an examiner can see the shape of the answer from the first line.
common_mistakes: Naming only one route. The question asks how plants synthesise amino acids in general.
Calling the second one 'deamination'. It is TRANSamination — a transfer, not a removal.
steps.memory_tip: One route builds the first amino acid; the other passes it on.

steps.label: Reductive amination
steps.margin_note: Equation plus the enzyme name. The guide prints NADPH-; the reductant is NADPH + H+.
lines: Ammonia reacts with alpha-ketoglutaric acid to
form the amino acid glutamic acid.
steps.why: This is where nitrogen first enters an organic molecule, so every other amino acid in the plant traces back to this one reaction.
common_mistakes: Writing the product as glutamine. The product here is GLUTAMIC ACID (glutamate).
Leaving out the enzyme. Glutamate dehydrogenase is part of the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Ammonia meets a keto acid and becomes an amino acid: the first nitrogen in.

steps.label: Transamination
steps.margin_note: Say what is transferred, from what, to what. Name glutamic acid as the donor.
lines: An amino group is transferred from an amino
acid to the keto group of a keto acid.
Glutamic acid is the main donor of the NH2
steps.why: Transamination makes every other amino acid by moving one group, so the plant needs the reductive amination step only once and can build the rest from it.
common_mistakes: Saying a new nitrogen atom is added. The SAME amino group is moved from one acid to another.
Forgetting that glutamic acid is the usual donor. That is what links the two routes.
steps.memory_tip: Transamination does not make nitrogen, it passes nitrogen along.

steps.label: The named enzymes
steps.margin_note: Both enzyme names on their own lines. Watch the spelling of transaminase.
lines: Between them the plant builds all twenty amino
steps.why: The two enzymes are the shortest correct summary of the whole answer, which is why they are worth stating once more on their own line.
common_mistakes: Writing 'transanimase'. The enzyme is TRANSAMINASE. The guide misprints it.
Naming no enzyme at all. Both enzyme names carry this mark.
steps.memory_tip: Dehydrogenase to start, transaminase to spread.
